items.summary: GitLab has a public story about deleting the wrong thing. In January 2017 an engineer who was trying to restore replication wiped a data directory they believed was on the secondary. It was on the primary. The postmortem they published afterwards is still one of the better things written about a database outage. At PGConf.EU in Valencia last week a few people from GitLab came to me with the inverse problem. They have one table, 4 TB, on a primary with ten replicas, and they want it gone, on purpose, with as little impact as they can manage. It's an archival table: nothing writes to it, and nothing is supposed to read it. DROP TABLE is the ob…
items.title: Radim Marek: Getting rid of a 4 TB table in PostgreSQL

items.summary: Read/write splitting is easy for single, autocommit statements. It gets hard the moment a client opens a transaction. Most proxies give up and send every statement inside a transaction to the primary, even the reads. This article is about a middle path we built into Polar Proxy: keep the transaction on the primary, but let its read statements borrow a replica connection.
items.title: Vadim Yatsenko: Splitting the Read-Only Transaction: Replica Reads Inside an Open Transaction
